title: A-Star Grid Navigator: Quiz Engine
description: A-Star Grid Navigator built as a quiz engine. A-star guides Dijkstra with a heuristic estimating remaining distance, exploring far fewer nodes when the heuristic is admissible. The navigator compares node expansions of Dijkstra, greedy, and A-star on obstacle grids with Manhattan and Euclidean heuristics. Good heuristics feel like cheating. A multiple-choice quiz engine that shuffles options deterministically, scores auto-answered or interactive sessions, and assigns letter grades.
resume_bullet: Built a A-Star Grid Navigator in Python with deterministic option shuffling, auto and interactive answering modes, and letter-grade scoring.

description: A/B Test Analyzer built as a report generator. Analyzing an A/B test goes beyond the p-value: the analyzer computes the lift with confidence intervals, checks sample-ratio mismatch (randomization health), runs sequential-valid methods if peeking occurred, and segments by platform. A report generator that builds seeded synthetic data, aggregates it, and writes a Markdown report with summary and per-service tables.

title: A/B Test Middleware: Monitoring Agent
description: A/B Test Middleware built as a Monitoring agent. A/B testing routes users into experiment variants consistently: the middleware hashes a user id into buckets, serves the assigned variant, and logs exposures for analysis. Sticky bucketing keeps users in one variant across sessions, and mutual exclusion prevents overlapping experiments from confounding. Guardrails pause tests on metric regressions. Samples synthetic topic metrics for N cycles, evaluates each reading against thresholds, prints readings and alerts.
resume_bullet: Built a A/B Test Middleware monitoring agent in Python (stdlib) sampling synthetic CPU, memory, and latency metrics on a fixed cadence; evaluates threshold breaches and prints readings with alerts and a summary.

Activation is the 'aha moment' quantified: the finder correlates early user actions with long-term retention to identify which behaviors predict staying. It tests candidate actions as classifiers of retained users. The winning metric becomes the onboarding team's north star input. A report generator that builds seeded synthetic data, aggregates it, and writes a Markdown report with summary and per-service tables.
resume_bullet: Built a Activation Metric Finder in Python that aggregates seeded measurement data into summary tables and emits a Markdown report.

title: Active Learning (Uncertainty Sampling): Data Pipeline (Etl)
description: Active Learning (Uncertainty Sampling) built as a Data pipeline (ETL). Active learning labels the most informative points first: uncertainty sampling queries points where the model is least confident, cutting labeling cost dramatically. The demo compares learning curves against random sampling. It is how teams label efficiently with expert annotators. Extracts synthetic topic records, transforms them (drop invalid, normalize, bucket), and loads the clean set to CSV.
resume_bullet: Built a Active Learning (Uncertainty Sampling) ETL pipeline in Python (stdlib csv) with extract, transform, and load stages; handles corrupt rows with drop counts and reports per-stage statistics to the console.

title: Activity Feed Aggregator: Data Pipeline (Etl)
description: Activity Feed Aggregator built as a Data pipeline (ETL). Social feeds merge many actors' actions into one timeline: the fan-out service collects events, ranks them (recency, affinity, type weights), dedupes, and paginates per user. Push fan-out precomputes feeds for active users while pull computes on read for the long tail. Ranking quality is the product. Extracts synthetic topic records, transforms them (drop invalid, normalize, bucket), and loads the clean set to CSV.

title: Activity Selection Scheduler: Command-Line Tool
description: Activity Selection Scheduler built as a Command-line tool. Picking the maximum number of non-overlapping activities is solved greedily by earliest finish time, and the proof is instructive. The scheduler shows the greedy picks versus brute force on small inputs. The rare case where greedy is provably optimal. A subcommand CLI that generates seeded synthetic topic rows and reports summaries, top-N rows, or filtered rows as tables or JSON.

title: AdaBoost (Weighted Voting): Decision Tree Classifier
description: AdaBoost (Weighted Voting) built as a Decision tree classifier. AdaBoost reweights training examples after each round so the next weak learner focuses on previous mistakes, then combines learners by weighted vote based on their accuracy. It turns slightly-better-than-chance stumps into a strong classifier. Noisy labels can make it chase outliers, which the demo shows clearly. Grows a Gini-based decision tree on seeded synthetic features, prints the tree as text, and reports test accuracy.
resume_bullet: Built a AdaBoost (Weighted Voting) decision tree classifier in pure Python using greedy Gini-impurity splits; demo prints the learned tree as text and reports test accuracy on a held-out split.

title: Adapter (Legacy Wrapper): Api Client Sim
description: Adapter (Legacy Wrapper) built as a API client sim. Adapters let incompatible interfaces collaborate: a wrapper translates a legacy library's API into the interface new code expects, without touching either side. It is the pragmatic pattern for technical debt: new code stays clean while old code keeps running. Two-way adapters sync both directions. A simulated REST API client that paginates through an in-process fake API, retrying simulated server errors with backoff.
resume_bullet: Built a Adapter (Legacy Wrapper) in Python with paginated fetching, retry-on-500 with backoff, and a full request history for debugging.

Anycast routes to the nearest of many same-address servers: the demo announces one prefix from multiple locations and shows clients reaching the topologically closest instance, with failover on outage. It is how DNS roots and CDNs achieve global low latency with one IP. A multiple-choice quiz engine that shuffles options deterministically, scores auto-answered or interactive sessions, and assigns letter grades.
resume_bullet: Built a Anycast Routing Demo in Python with deterministic option shuffling, auto and interactive answering modes, and letter-grade scoring.

title: API Abuse Rate Detector: Log Analyzer
description: API Abuse Rate Detector built as a Log analyzer. Legitimate API clients behave predictably while scrapers and attackers hammer endpoints at inhuman rates or probe for IDOR patterns. The detector profiles per-key request rates, endpoint entropy, and error ratios, flagging keys whose behavior diverges from their historical norm. It separates a viral launch from an attack by looking at error and spread patterns. title: API Key Authentication Service: Config Manager
description: API Key Authentication Service built as a config manager. API keys are the simplest service-to-service credential: the server issues random high-entropy keys, stores only their hashes, and checks the presented key on each request. Keys carry scopes, expiry, and per-key rate limits, and rotation issues a replacement while the old one stays valid briefly. The hard parts are secure storage, revocation propagation, and never logging the raw key. A layered configuration manager that merges defaults, an INI snippet, environment variables, and CLI overrides with type checking and validation.
resume_bullet: Built a API Key Authentication Service in Python with four-layer precedence, typed coercion, per-key source tracking, and schema validation.

title: Autosave Draft Service: Lru Cache
description: Autosave Draft Service built as a LRU cache. Autosave protects work from crashes: the client debounces edits, the service stores drafts keyed by user and document, and on reopen offers to restore the newer draft. Conflict handling decides when the draft diverges from a collaborator's newer save. Debounce tuning balances write load against data-loss windows. A fixed-capacity LRU cache that evicts the least-recently-used entry and reports hit, miss, and eviction statistics.
resume_bullet: Implemented a Autosave Draft Service in Python on an OrderedDict with O(1) get/put and hit/miss/eviction instrumentation.

When thousands of tests run, controlling false discovery rate (expected fraction of false positives among rejections) beats family-wise control for power: BH sorts p-values and finds the largest k with p_k <= k/m * q. The demo shows BH discovering real effects Bonferroni would miss. A report generator that builds seeded synthetic data, aggregates it, and writes a Markdown report with summary and per-service tables.
resume_bullet: Built a Benjamini-Hochberg FDR Control in Python that aggregates seeded measurement data into summary tables and emits a Markdown report.

title: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR Control: Simulation (Logistic Growth)
description: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR Control built as a Simulation (logistic growth). When thousands of tests run, controlling false discovery rate (expected fraction of false positives among rejections) beats family-wise control for power: BH sorts p-values and finds the largest k with p_k <= k/m * q. The demo shows BH discovering real effects Bonferroni would miss. Euler-integrates logistic growth dP/dt = r*P*(1-P/K) and prints the trajectory table with summary statistics.
resume_bullet: Built a Benjamini-Hochberg FDR Control simulator in Python (stdlib) implementing Euler integration of logistic growth with seeded parameters; demo runs end-to-end and prints the trajectory table with summary statistics.

title: Backend-for-Frontend Request Aggregator: Api Client Sim
description: Backend-for-Frontend Request Aggregator built as a API client sim. Mobile and web clients need different data shapes, so a BFF aggregates: one client call fans out to several microservices in parallel, and the aggregator merges, reshapes, and trims the responses into the exact payload the UI needs. Timeouts and partial-failure policies decide what the client sees when one service is slow. It trades backend chattiness for client simplicity. A simulated REST API client that paginates through an in-process fake API, retrying simulated server errors with backoff.
resume_bullet: Built a Backend-for-Frontend Request Aggregator in Python with paginated fetching, retry-on-500 with backoff, and a full request history for debugging.

title: Bonferroni Correction: Quiz Engine
description: Bonferroni Correction built as a quiz engine. title: Bridge (Notifier Channels): Api Client Sim
description: Bridge (Notifier Channels) built as a API client sim. Bridge separates abstraction from implementation so both vary independently: notifiers (alert, reminder) work over channels (email, SMS, push) in a matrix, not a class explosion. Adding a channel means one new class, not N notifier subclasses. It tames two-dimensional variation. A simulated REST API client that paginates through an in-process fake API, retrying simulated server errors with backoff.
resume_bullet: Built a Bridge (Notifier Channels) in Python with paginated fetching, retry-on-500 with backoff, and a full request history for debugging.

title: Broken Link Crawler: Api Client Sim
description: Broken Link Crawler built as a API client sim. Link rot erodes trust, so the crawler fetches a site's pages, extracts links, and checks each target's status with HEAD requests, respecting robots.txt and rate limits. It reports broken links grouped by source page and distinguishes 404s from timeouts and redirect chains. Politeness (crawl delay, concurrency caps) keeps it from becoming an accidental DDoS. A simulated REST API client that paginates through an in-process fake API, retrying simulated server errors with backoff.

title: Chain of Responsibility (Validators): Command-Line Tool
description: Chain of Responsibility (Validators) built as a Command-line tool. A handler chain passes requests along until one handles them: validators check a request in sequence, each either passing or rejecting with its error. title: Checkout State Machine: Rest Api Service
description: Checkout State Machine built as a REST API service. Checkout is a state machine (cart, address, shipping, payment, review, placed) where each transition validates its step and the machine guards against skipping or replaying steps. Payment attempts are idempotent so double-clicks cannot double-charge. Failed payments return to the payment step with the error, never losing the cart. Serves a small JSON REST API for the topic records, with health, list, create, and stats endpoints.
resume_bullet: Built a Checkout State Machine REST API in Python (stdlib http.server) with JSON endpoints, an in-memory store, and a threaded self-test that exercises every route via urllib; demo binds 127.0.0.1, verifies all endpoints, and exits cleanly.

title: Checkpoint and Recovery (ARIES-lite): Backup Tool
description: Checkpoint and Recovery (ARIES-lite) built as a backup tool. ARIES recovery replays the WAL in three passes: analysis finds dirty pages and active transactions, redo repeats history, undo rolls back losers. Checkpoints bound the replay work. The lite version implements the three passes on a page model. It is the algorithm that made crash recovery boring (in a good way). A backup tool that copies a folder, records SHA-256 checksums in a JSON manifest, and verifies the backup by re-hashing.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, hashlib, json, os, random, shutil
resume_bullet: Built a Checkpoint and Recovery (ARIES-lite) in Python that copies a folder tree and verifies integrity with SHA-256 checksums stored in a JSON manifest.

Shared cursors show where collaborators are: the broker relays cursor positions and selections per document at throttled rates, assigns deterministic colors per user, and removes cursors on disconnect. Positions reference document versions so they stay meaningful during concurrent edits. It is presence applied to a document. A loopback-only TCP chat server that relays messages between clients, with a default self-test that verifies delivery end to end.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, random, socket, threading, time
resume_bullet: Built a Collaborative Cursor Broker in Python with sockets and threads, including a scripted two-client self-test that verifies message relay.

title: Content-Addressable Asset Store: Backup Tool
description: Content-Addressable Asset Store built as a backup tool. Content addressing names files by their hash: identical content dedupes automatically, and the hash doubles as an integrity check on every read. The store shards blobs by hash prefix, serves them with immutable cache headers, and garbage-collects unreferenced blobs. It is how CDNs and caches get infinite cache lifetimes safely. A backup tool that copies a folder, records SHA-256 checksums in a JSON manifest, and verifies the backup by re-hashing.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, hashlib, json, os, random, shutil
resume_bullet: Built a Content-Addressable Asset Store in Python that copies a folder tree and verifies integrity with SHA-256 checksums stored in a JSON manifest.

description: Content Negotiation Engine built as a API client sim. CSP is a whitelist telling the browser exactly where scripts, styles, images, and frames may load from, which neuters most XSS payloads. The builder composes directives from an asset inventory, generates nonces or hashes for legitimate inline scripts, and parses violation reports to find what would break. Rolling it out in report-only mode first avoids self-inflicted outages. A layered configuration manager that merges defaults, an INI snippet, environment variables, and CLI overrides with type checking and validation.
resume_bullet: Built a Content Security Policy Builder in Python with four-layer precedence, typed coercion, per-key source tracking, and schema validation.

title: CSRF Token Protection: Encryption Tool
description: CSRF Token Protection built as a Encryption tool. Cross-site request forgery tricks a logged-in browser into submitting a form on another site, riding the victim's cookies. The defense issues a per-session CSRF token, embeds it in forms, and requires it on state-changing requests; same-site cookie attributes add a second layer. Decision trees split data recursively on the feature and threshold that most reduces impurity (Gini or entropy), producing human-readable if-then rules. Building one from scratch means implementing the split search, stopping criteria, and leaf prediction. Trees overfit eagerly, which is why depth limits exist. Draws a seeded synthetic sample and reports count, mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and an ASCII histogram.
resume_bullet: Built a Decision Tree (Gini Splits) statistical analyzer in pure Python computing mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and histograms from seeded synthetic data; prints a formatted report with an ASCII distribution plot.

title: Decision Tree Pruning: Decision Tree Classifier
description: Decision Tree Pruning built as a Decision tree classifier. Fully grown trees memorize noise, so pruning trades tree size for generalization: cost-complexity pruning penalizes leaf count and picks the subtree minimizing penalized validation error. Pre-pruning (depth limits) is cruder; post-pruning usually wins. The pruning path shows the whole accuracy-vs-size frontier. Grows a Gini-based decision tree on seeded synthetic features, prints the tree as text, and reports test accuracy.
resume_bullet: Built a Decision Tree Pruning decision tree classifier in pure Python using greedy Gini-impurity splits; demo prints the learned tree as text and reports test accuracy on a held-out split.

The forecaster evaluates with bias-aware metrics (not just MAPE) and produces intervals for safety stock. Forecast value added tracks whether complexity beats naive. Draws a seeded synthetic sample and reports count, mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and an ASCII histogram.
resume_bullet: Built a Demand Forecaster statistical analyzer in pure Python computing mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and histograms from seeded synthetic data; prints a formatted report with an ASCII distribution plot.

title: Denoising Autoencoder: Quiz Engine
description: Denoising Autoencoder built as a quiz engine. Autoencoders compress input through a bottleneck and reconstruct it; denoising variants train on corrupted inputs, forcing the network to learn robust structure rather than the identity. Reconstruction error then flags anomalies. The bottleneck size controls the compression. A multiple-choice quiz engine that shuffles options deterministically, scores auto-answered or interactive sessions, and assigns letter grades.
resume_bullet: Built a Denoising Autoencoder in Python with deterministic option shuffling, auto and interactive answering modes, and letter-grade scoring.

description: Denormalization Advisor built as a report generator. title: Distributed Tracing Sampler: Log Analyzer
description: Distributed Tracing Sampler built as a Log analyzer. Tracing every request is too expensive, so samplers decide which traces to keep: head-based sampling decides at request start (fast, but misses interesting tails), tail-based sampling buffers and keeps traces with errors or high latency. The sampler propagates trace context (traceparent) across services either way. Sampling strategy determines what you can debug later. Generates a synthetic service log in memory, parses each line with a regex, and reports level/service counts, top errors, and error rate.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, random, re, collections, datetime
resume_bullet: Built a Distributed Tracing Sampler log analyzer in Python (stdlib re) generating a synthetic service log in memory, parsing it with a named-group regex, and reporting level and service counts with top error messages.

title: DNS Cache with TTL: Lru Cache
description: DNS Cache with TTL built as a LRU cache. DNS caching obeys TTLs: the cache stores records until expiry, serves stale-while-revalidate during refresh, and honors negative caching for NXDOMAIN. TTL choice trades propagation speed against query load. It is why DNS changes 'take time'. A fixed-capacity LRU cache that evicts the least-recently-used entry and reports hit, miss, and eviction statistics.
resume_bullet: Implemented a DNS Cache with TTL in Python on an OrderedDict with O(1) get/put and hit/miss/eviction instrumentation.

title: DNS Tunneling Detector: Command-Line Tool
description: DNS Tunneling Detector built as a Command-line tool. DNS tunneling smuggles data out of a network by encoding it in subdomain labels of DNS queries, abusing a protocol that firewalls almost always allow. The detector scores queries on label entropy, query length, request frequency, and the rarity of the queried domain, because tunneled traffic looks random and chatty compared with human browsing. title: Double-Submit Cookie CSRF Defense: Encryption Tool
description: Double-Submit Cookie CSRF Defense built as a Encryption tool. The double-submit pattern avoids server-side CSRF state: the server sets a random token in a cookie and the client must echo the same value in a header or form field, which a cross-site attacker cannot read due to the same-origin policy. Validation compares the two values in constant time. It pairs naturally with JWT-based stateless auth. Encrypts and decrypts data with a hand-written XOR stream cipher using a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream.
resume_bullet: Built a Double-Submit Cookie CSRF Defense encryption tool in Python (stdlib hashlib) implementing an XOR stream cipher with a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream; demo performs a full encrypt/decrypt round trip and verifies the result.

title: ETag Conditional GET Cache: Lru Cache
description: ETag Conditional GET Cache built as a LRU cache. Conditional GETs let caches revalidate cheaply: the client sends If-None-Match with its cached ETag and the server replies 304 when the representation is unchanged. Strong ETags change on any byte difference; weak ETags ignore insignificant changes. The cache layer must also forward revalidation correctly and respect Vary. A fixed-capacity LRU cache that evicts the least-recently-used entry and reports hit, miss, and eviction statistics.

description: Extremely Randomized Trees built as a Decision tree classifier. Extra Trees push randomization further than random forests: split thresholds are chosen randomly rather than optimally, making training much faster and often reducing variance more. title: File Integrity Monitor: Backup Tool
description: File Integrity Monitor built as a backup tool. Rootkits and intruders modify system binaries and configs, so a file integrity monitor keeps cryptographic hashes of watched files and re-checks them on a schedule. Any hash mismatch, permission change, or unexpected new file in a watched directory raises an alert with the diff of what changed. The baseline database itself is checksummed so tampering with the monitor is detectable. A backup tool that copies a folder, records SHA-256 checksums in a JSON manifest, and verifies the backup by re-hashing.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, hashlib, json, os, random, shutil
resume_bullet: Built a File Integrity Monitor in Python that copies a folder tree and verifies integrity with SHA-256 checksums stored in a JSON manifest.

Firewall policies are ordered rule lists where the first match wins, and a misplaced permissive rule can silently shadow stricter ones below it. The simulator evaluates packets against a rule set, shows exactly which rule matched and why, and audits the policy for shadowed rules, overly broad allows, and default-deny gaps. It lets engineers test policy changes safely before pushing them to production. Euler-integrates logistic growth dP/dt = r*P*(1-P/K) and prints the trajectory table with summary statistics.
resume_bullet: Built a Firewall Rule Simulator simulator in Python (stdlib) implementing Euler integration of logistic growth with seeded parameters; demo runs end-to-end and prints the trajectory table with summary statistics.

Point forecasts hide uncertainty: quantile regression estimates prediction intervals (e.g., 10th/90th percentiles) so planners see the range. Pinball loss trains the quantiles; coverage calibration checks the 80% interval really covers 80%. Inventory and capacity planning run on intervals, not points. Draws a seeded synthetic sample and reports count, mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and an ASCII histogram.
resume_bullet: Built a Forecast Intervals via Quantiles statistical analyzer in pure Python computing mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and histograms from seeded synthetic data; prints a formatted report with an ASCII distribution plot.

title: IP Fragmentation and Reassembly: Port Scanner
description: IP Fragmentation and Reassembly built as a port scanner. Packets bigger than the MTU fragment: the demo splits datagrams with correct offsets and MF flags, then reassembles at the receiver handling out-of-order and overlapping fragments. It shows why path-MTU discovery tries to avoid fragmentation. Overlapping fragments are also a classic IDS evasion. A loopback-only TCP port scanner that reports open/closed state and latency, and refuses any non-loopback target.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, concurrent.futures, random, socket, sys, time
resume_bullet: Built a IP Fragmentation and Reassembly in Python using parallel TCP connects, restricted to loopback targets with a self-test that validates scan accuracy.

description: Fuzzy Duplicate Matcher built as a Data pipeline (ETL). title: Gaussian Mixture Models (EM): K-Means Clustering
description: Gaussian Mixture Models (EM) built as a K-means clustering. GMMs model data as a weighted sum of Gaussians, fit by expectation-maximization: the E-step computes soft cluster responsibilities, the M-step updates means, covariances, and weights. Soft assignments handle overlapping clusters where k-means' hard assignments fail. BIC selects the component count. Runs Lloyd's k-means on seeded 2-D synthetic points and prints final centroids, cluster sizes, and inertia.
resume_bullet: Built a Gaussian Mixture Models (EM) k-means clustering tool in pure Python implementing Lloyd's algorithm (nearest-centroid assignment, mean recomputation) on seeded synthetic data; demo prints centroids, cluster sizes, and inertia.

title: Hashing Trick Vectorizer: Data Pipeline (Etl)
description: Hashing Trick Vectorizer built as a Data pipeline (ETL). title: Inventory Reservation (Hold with TTL): Rest Api Service
description: Inventory Reservation (Hold with TTL) built as a REST API service. Selling the last item twice is a classic bug: reservation places a TTL hold on stock at checkout start, decrements on payment success, and releases on timeout or cancellation. The hold table must handle concurrency with atomic compare-and-set. Oversell protection is the whole point. Serves a small JSON REST API for the topic records, with health, list, create, and stats endpoints.

The detector graphs authentication events between hosts, flagging unusual edges like a workstation logging into a domain controller or rapid fan-out to many hosts. It catches the spread phase of intrusions. Samples synthetic topic metrics for N cycles, evaluates each reading against thresholds, prints readings and alerts.
resume_bullet: Built a Lateral Movement Detector monitoring agent in Python (stdlib) sampling synthetic CPU, memory, and latency metrics on a fixed cadence; evaluates threshold breaches and prints readings with alerts and a summary.

resume_bullet: Built a Lateral Movement Detector statistical analyzer in pure Python computing mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and histograms from seeded synthetic data; prints a formatted report with an ASCII distribution plot.

title: Layered Architecture Demo: Command-Line Tool

description: Leaderboard Service built as a LRU cache. Learning curves plot train and validation error against training-set size: both high means high bias (underfit), a gap means high variance (overfit). The diagnosis prescribes the fix: more data helps variance, more capacity helps bias. It is the first plot to draw when a model disappoints. Draws a seeded synthetic sample and reports count, mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and an ASCII histogram.
resume_bullet: Built a Learning Curve Diagnoser statistical analyzer in pure Python computing mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and histograms from seeded synthetic data; prints a formatted report with an ASCII distribution plot.

title: Learning Rate Schedulers: Task Scheduler
description: Learning Rate Schedulers built as a Task scheduler. Learning-rate schedules (step decay, cosine annealing, warmup) start fast and finish precise: large early steps explore, small late steps settle into minima. Warmup avoids early instability in big models. The scheduler is often worth more than the optimizer choice. Registers interval jobs on a heap scheduler, runs them for a fixed demo duration, and prints the execution log.
resume_bullet: Built a Learning Rate Schedulers interval scheduler in Python (stdlib heapq) with drift-free rescheduling; demo registers jobs on sub-second intervals, runs them, and prints a timestamped execution log.

title: Least-Connections Load Balancer: Monitoring Agent
description: Least-Connections Load Balancer built as a Monitoring agent. Least-connections routing sends each request to the backend with fewest active connections: better than round-robin when requests vary in cost. The balancer tracks active counts and handles ties. It adapts to heterogeneous backends without configuration. Samples synthetic topic metrics for N cycles, evaluates each reading against thresholds, prints readings and alerts.

title: Long-Polling Fallback Transport: Api Client Sim
description: Long-Polling Fallback Transport built as a API client sim. Where WebSockets are blocked, long polling emulates push: the client holds a request open until the server has data or a timeout fires, then immediately re-issues it. The server needs per-client queues, timeout management, and message ordering so nothing is lost between polls. It is less efficient than a persistent socket but works through the most restrictive proxies. A simulated REST API client that paginates through an in-process fake API, retrying simulated server errors with backoff.
resume_bullet: Built a Long-Polling Fallback Transport in Python with paginated fetching, retry-on-500 with backoff, and a full request history for debugging.

Markdown gives writers plain-text formatting that renders to HTML: the renderer tokenizes headings, emphasis, links, code spans, lists, and blockquotes, then emits sanitized HTML. It must escape raw HTML by default and handle nested constructs like links inside emphasis. A table extension shows how renderers grow new syntax. A report generator that builds seeded synthetic data, aggregates it, and writes a Markdown report with summary and per-service tables.
resume_bullet: Built a Markdown to HTML Renderer in Python that aggregates seeded measurement data into summary tables and emits a Markdown report.

title: Markowitz Portfolio Optimizer: Linear Regression
description: Markowitz Portfolio Optimizer built as a Linear regression. Markowitz balances return against risk: the optimizer finds minimum-variance portfolios for target returns via quadratic programming (lite: grid over weights or analytical two-asset), tracing the efficient frontier. The Sharpe-maximizing tangency portfolio is the headline result. Estimation error is the practical enemy. Fits y = slope*x + intercept by closed-form least squares on seeded synthetic data and reports coefficients, R^2, and predictions.
resume_bullet: Built a Markowitz Portfolio Optimizer linear regression in pure Python implementing closed-form least squares on seeded synthetic data; demo recovers known coefficients and reports R^2 with a prediction table.

title: Memento (Snapshot): Backup Tool
description: Memento (Snapshot) built as a backup tool. Mementos capture state for later restore without exposing internals: the originator creates snapshots, the caretaker stores them, and restore rolls back. It powers undo across complex state. Snapshot frequency trades memory against undo granularity. A backup tool that copies a folder, records SHA-256 checksums in a JSON manifest, and verifies the backup by re-hashing.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, hashlib, json, os, random, shutil
resume_bullet: Built a Memento (Snapshot) in Python that copies a folder tree and verifies integrity with SHA-256 checksums stored in a JSON manifest.

title: Miller-Rabin Primality: Encryption Tool
description: Miller-Rabin Primality built as a Encryption tool. Miller-Rabin tests primality probabilistically: composites are caught with probability 3/4 per round, so enough rounds mean practical certainty. The tool runs rounds on candidates showing witnesses, and compares against deterministic trial division. How crypto finds its primes. Encrypts and decrypts data with a hand-written XOR stream cipher using a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream.
resume_bullet: Built a Miller-Rabin Primality encryption tool in Python (stdlib hashlib) implementing an XOR stream cipher with a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream; demo performs a full encrypt/decrypt round trip and verifies the result.

Non-negative matrix factorization splits a matrix into non-negative parts, yielding interpretable components (faces into eyes/noses, users into taste profiles). Multiplicative updates keep everything non-negative. The parts-based representation is NMF's signature advantage over SVD. Draws a seeded synthetic sample and reports count, mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and an ASCII histogram.
resume_bullet: Built a NMF Parts-Based Decomposition statistical analyzer in pure Python computing mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and histograms from seeded synthetic data; prints a formatted report with an ASCII distribution plot.

title: Neural Net Early Stopping: Task Scheduler
description: Neural Net Early Stopping built as a Task scheduler. Neural nets overfit fast, so early stopping with patience and best-weight restoration is standard: it stops training when validation loss plateaus. Combined with learning-rate schedules it is the cheapest regularization available. The demo tunes patience on noisy validation curves. Registers interval jobs on a heap scheduler, runs them for a fixed demo duration, and prints the execution log.
resume_bullet: Built a Neural Net Early Stopping interval scheduler in Python (stdlib heapq) with drift-free rescheduling; demo registers jobs on sub-second intervals, runs them, and prints a timestamped execution log.

title: Neural Net Early Stopping: Simulation (Logistic Growth)

title: One-Hot Encoder: Command-Line Tool
description: One-Hot Encoder built as a Command-line tool. One-hot encoding turns categories into binary columns so linear models can use them: each category gets its own 0/1 column, with the first often dropped to avoid collinearity. High-cardinality features explode dimensionality, which motivates hashing or target encoding. Unseen categories at predict time need a defined policy. A subcommand CLI that generates seeded synthetic topic rows and reports summaries, top-N rows, or filtered rows as tables or JSON.
resume_bullet: Built a One-Hot Encoder CLI tool in Python (argparse subcommands) over seeded synthetic data with table and JSON output; runs summary, top-N, and filter reports deterministically.

title: Operational Transform (Lite): Chat Server
description: Operational Transform (Lite) built as a chat server. Collaborative editing needs conflict resolution: operational transform rewrites concurrent operations (insert/delete) so all clients converge on the same text. The core is the transform function adjusting positions when operations overlap. A central server orders operations, and clients transform their pending ops against incoming ones. A loopback-only TCP chat server that relays messages between clients, with a default self-test that verifies delivery end to end.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, random, socket, threading, time
resume_bullet: Built a Operational Transform (Lite) in Python with sockets and threads, including a scripted two-client self-test that verifies message relay.

title: Optimistic UI Conflict Resolver: Rest Api Service
description: Optimistic UI Conflict Resolver built as a REST API service. Optimistic UI applies changes instantly and reconciles with the server after: the resolver tracks pending mutations, rolls back on server rejection, and merges when the server state moved underneath. Version vectors or etags detect the conflicts. Done well, apps feel instant; done poorly, user edits vanish mysteriously. Serves a small JSON REST API for the topic records, with health, list, create, and stats endpoints.
resume_bullet: Built a Optimistic UI Conflict Resolver REST API in Python (stdlib http.server) with JSON endpoints, an in-memory store, and a threaded self-test that exercises every route via urllib; demo binds 127.0.0.1, verifies all endpoints, and exits cleanly.

Non-production environments should not hold real PII: the masker scans columns for PII patterns (emails, SSNs, cards), applies format-preserving masking or tokenization, and keeps referential consistency across tables. It enables safe analytics on production-shaped data. Encrypts and decrypts data with a hand-written XOR stream cipher using a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream.
resume_bullet: Built a PII Data Masking encryption tool in Python (stdlib hashlib) implementing an XOR stream cipher with a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream; demo performs a full encrypt/decrypt round trip and verifies the result.

The checker evaluates budgets against current replica counts, simulating drains to prove minimum availability holds. It catches the budget that allows zero disruptions or permits too many. A layered configuration manager that merges defaults, an INI snippet, environment variables, and CLI overrides with type checking and validation.
resume_bullet: Built a Pod Disruption Budget Checker in Python with four-layer precedence, typed coercion, per-key source tracking, and schema validation.

title: Policy Iteration (Small MDP): Quiz Engine
description: Policy Iteration (Small MDP) built as a quiz engine. Policy iteration alternates policy evaluation (solving Bellman equations) and policy improvement (greedy updates) until the policy stops changing, converging to optimal in few iterations for small MDPs. It is the exact dynamic-programming solution that learning algorithms approximate. The demo runs it on tiny MDPs where exactness is checkable. A multiple-choice quiz engine that shuffles options deterministically, scores auto-answered or interactive sessions, and assigns letter grades.
resume_bullet: Built a Policy Iteration (Small MDP) in Python with deterministic option shuffling, auto and interactive answering modes, and letter-grade scoring.

title: Poll Voting Service: Rest Api Service
description: Poll Voting Service built as a REST API service. Online polls need one-person-one-vote-ish: the service dedupes by voter id with cookie/IP fallbacks, supports single vs ranked vs approval ballots, and tallies with methods like instant-runoff. title: Polynomial Feature Expansion: Linear Regression
description: Polynomial Feature Expansion built as a Linear regression. Linear models can fit curves if you first expand features into polynomial terms: x becomes [x, x^2, x^3], and OLS fits the rest. Degree controls flexibility, and high degrees overfit wildly without regularization. It is the simplest way to see the bias-variance trade-off in action. Fits y = slope*x + intercept by closed-form least squares on seeded synthetic data and reports coefficients, R^2, and predictions.
resume_bullet: Built a Polynomial Feature Expansion linear regression in pure Python implementing closed-form least squares on seeded synthetic data; demo recovers known coefficients and reports R^2 with a prediction table.

title: Post-Stratification Weighter: Report Generator
description: Post-Stratification Weighter built as a report generator. Surveys rarely match the population: post-stratification reweights respondents to known population margins (raking iterates to match multiple margins). A report generator that builds seeded synthetic data, aggregates it, and writes a Markdown report with summary and per-service tables.

title: Web Push Subscription Manager: Encryption Tool
description: Web Push Subscription Manager built as a Encryption tool. Web push delivers notifications even when the tab is closed: the manager stores push subscriptions (endpoint + VAPID keys), encrypts payloads per the Web Push protocol, and prunes expired (410) subscriptions. title: QoS Priority Queue (DiffServ-lite): Monitoring Agent
description: QoS Priority Queue (DiffServ-lite) built as a Monitoring agent. QoS prioritizes by class: the lite DiffServ model marks packets (voice, video, best-effort) and schedules with strict priority or weighted fair queueing, policing ingress rates. title: Read Receipt Tracker: Chat Server
description: Read Receipt Tracker built as a chat server. Read receipts confirm delivery and reading: the tracker records sent/delivered/read transitions per message per recipient, handles group-chat partial reads, and respects users who disable receipts. Timestamps on each transition feed 'seen by' UIs. Privacy settings complicate the state machine in interesting ways. A loopback-only TCP chat server that relays messages between clients, with a default self-test that verifies delivery end to end.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, random, socket, threading, time
resume_bullet: Built a Read Receipt Tracker in Python with sockets and threads, including a scripted two-client self-test that verifies message relay.

title: Recommendation Widget (Also Viewed): Data Pipeline (Etl)
description: Recommendation Widget (Also Viewed) built as a Data pipeline (ETL). Also-viewed widgets mine co-occurrence: items frequently viewed in the same sessions get linked, scored by lift over random chance. The batch job builds the item graph nightly while the widget serves precomputed neighbors with fallbacks to popular items for cold starts. It is the simplest recommender that actually lifts conversion. Extracts synthetic topic records, transforms them (drop invalid, normalize, bucket), and loads the clean set to CSV.
resume_bullet: Built a Recommendation Widget (Also Viewed) ETL pipeline in Python (stdlib csv) with extract, transform, and load stages; handles corrupt rows with drop counts and reports per-stage statistics to the console.

description: Remember-Me Token Rotation built as a Encryption tool. title: Request Coalescing (Singleflight): Lru Cache
description: Request Coalescing (Singleflight) built as a LRU cache. When a cache entry expires, hundreds of concurrent requests can stampede the backend recomputing it: singleflight coalescing lets the first request do the work while the rest wait on the same in-flight call and share its result. The registry keys in-flight calls, attaches waiters, and propagates errors or cancellations to all of them. It turns a thundering herd into one backend call. A fixed-capacity LRU cache that evicts the least-recently-used entry and reports hit, miss, and eviction statistics.

The penalty strength lambda trades bias against variance: larger lambda means simpler, more stable models. The closed form just adds lambda to the diagonal of the Gram matrix. Fits y = slope*x + intercept by closed-form least squares on seeded synthetic data and reports coefficients, R^2, and predictions.
resume_bullet: Built a Ridge Regression (L2) linear regression in pure Python implementing closed-form least squares on seeded synthetic data; demo recovers known coefficients and reports R^2 with a prediction table.

title: Server-Sent Events Feed: Chat Server
description: Server-Sent Events Feed built as a chat server. Server-Sent Events give the server a one-way push channel over plain HTTP: the client opens an EventSource and the server streams text/event-stream messages with event types, ids, and retry hints. Automatic reconnection with Last-Event-ID lets clients resume where they left off after a drop. SSE is simpler than WebSockets whenever the client never needs to send messages back. title: Shapley Value Demo: Quiz Engine
description: Shapley Value Demo built as a quiz engine. Shapley values fairly attribute a prediction among features using cooperative game theory: each feature's marginal contribution averaged over all orderings. Exact computation is exponential, so the demo runs small-n exact and sampling approximations. It is the principled answer to 'which feature mattered'. A multiple-choice quiz engine that shuffles options deterministically, scores auto-answered or interactive sessions, and assigns letter grades.

title: Signed URL Generator (Presigned URLs): Encryption Tool
description: Signed URL Generator (Presigned URLs) built as a Encryption tool. Presigned URLs grant time-limited access to private objects without proxying bytes: the server signs the object key, expiry, and allowed method with HMAC, and the storage backend verifies the signature on arrival. The generator sets content-disposition and content-type constraints inside the signature so they cannot be tampered with. Leaked URLs simply expire. Encrypts and decrypts data with a hand-written XOR stream cipher using a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream.
resume_bullet: Built a Signed URL Generator (Presigned URLs) encryption tool in Python (stdlib hashlib) implementing an XOR stream cipher with a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream; demo performs a full encrypt/decrypt round trip and verifies the result.

title: Silhouette Score Evaluator: K-Means Clustering
description: Silhouette Score Evaluator built as a K-means clustering. The silhouette score measures clustering quality per point: how much closer it is to its own cluster than to the nearest other cluster, averaged over the data. Scores near 1 mean tight, separated clusters; near 0 mean overlap. It lets you compare k values or algorithms without ground truth. Runs Lloyd's k-means on seeded 2-D synthetic points and prints final centroids, cluster sizes, and inertia.
resume_bullet: Built a Silhouette Score Evaluator k-means clustering tool in pure Python implementing Lloyd's algorithm (nearest-centroid assignment, mean recomputation) on seeded synthetic data; demo prints centroids, cluster sizes, and inertia.

title: Vector Clocks (Causality Tracking): Chat Server
description: Vector Clocks (Causality Tracking) built as a chat server. Vector clocks track causality across replicas: each node counts its own events, merges take element-wise max, and comparison reveals happened-before, concurrent, or comparable. Concurrent writes become siblings to resolve. It is the honest alternative to wall-clock ordering. A loopback-only TCP chat server that relays messages between clients, with a default self-test that verifies delivery end to end.

description: WebSocket Backpressure Controller built as a chat server. Initialization decides whether deep networks train at all: zeros symmetry-break nothing, large random values saturate, while Xavier/He scaling keeps activation variances stable across layers. The demo trains identical networks from different inits and watches some fail. It is a five-line change with outsized impact. Draws a seeded synthetic sample and reports count, mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and an ASCII histogram.
resume_bullet: Built a Weight Initialization Effects statistical analyzer in pure Python computing mean, median, stdev, quartiles, and histograms from seeded synthetic data; prints a formatted report with an ASCII distribution plot.

title: What-If Scenario Simulator: Simulation (Logistic Growth)
description: What-If Scenario Simulator built as a Simulation (logistic growth). Scenarios ask 'what if price drops 10%': the simulator perturbs drivers through an estimated response model, propagating uncertainty via Monte Carlo to show outcome distributions, not points. Sensitivity tornado charts rank driver importance. It turns models into decision tools. Euler-integrates logistic growth dP/dt = r*P*(1-P/K) and prints the trajectory table with summary statistics.
resume_bullet: Built a What-If Scenario Simulator simulator in Python (stdlib) implementing Euler integration of logistic growth with seeded parameters; demo runs end-to-end and prints the trajectory table with summary statistics.

title: White-Label Theme Service: Config Manager
description: White-Label Theme Service built as a config manager. White-label products reskin per customer: the theme service resolves the tenant's brand (colors, logos, fonts, copy overrides), serves themed assets with caching, and falls back to defaults for missing keys. Theme validation keeps contrast accessible. It lets one codebase wear many brands. A layered configuration manager that merges defaults, an INI snippet, environment variables, and CLI overrides with type checking and validation.
resume_bullet: Built a White-Label Theme Service in Python with four-layer precedence, typed coercion, per-key source tracking, and schema validation.

title: Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test: Quiz Engine
description: Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test built as a quiz engine. The signed-rank test is the paired, nonparametric counterpart: it ranks absolute differences and sums signed ranks, testing median difference without normality. Ties and zeros need careful handling. It rescues paired analyses on skewed outcomes. A multiple-choice quiz engine that shuffles options deterministically, scores auto-answered or interactive sessions, and assigns letter grades.
resume_bullet: Built a Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test in Python with deterministic option shuffling, auto and interactive answering modes, and letter-grade scoring.

title: Window Functions Engine: Command-Line Tool
description: Window Functions Engine built as a Command-line tool. Window functions compute across row frames without collapsing groups: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, running sums, and LAG/LEAD over PARTITION BY and ORDER BY. The engine sorts partitions and evaluates frames. They answer 'top-N per group' and period-over-period in one pass. A subcommand CLI that generates seeded synthetic topic rows and reports summaries, top-N rows, or filtered rows as tables or JSON.
resume_bullet: Built a Window Functions Engine CLI tool in Python (argparse subcommands) over seeded synthetic data with table and JSON output; runs summary, top-N, and filter reports deterministically.

title: Write-Ahead Log (WAL): Backup Tool
description: Write-Ahead Log (WAL) built as a backup tool. Durability starts with the WAL: changes append to the log before touching data pages, so crashes replay the log to recover. The demo implements append, checkpoint, and replay, then crash-tests recovery. Group commit batches the fsync cost. No WAL, no durability guarantees. A backup tool that copies a folder, records SHA-256 checksums in a JSON manifest, and verifies the backup by re-hashing.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, hashlib, json, os, random, shutil
resume_bullet: Built a Write-Ahead Log (WAL) in Python that copies a folder tree and verifies integrity with SHA-256 checksums stored in a JSON manifest.

title: Z-Score Anomaly Detector: Monitoring Agent
description: Z-Score Anomaly Detector built as a Monitoring agent. The z-score flags points more than k standard deviations from the mean, the simplest anomaly rule there is. Robust variants use median and MAD so outliers cannot mask themselves by inflating the standard deviation. Rolling windows adapt it to drifting streams. Samples synthetic topic metrics for N cycles, evaluates each reading against thresholds, prints readings and alerts.
resume_bullet: Built a Z-Score Anomaly Detector monitoring agent in Python (stdlib) sampling synthetic CPU, memory, and latency metrics on a fixed cadence; evaluates threshold breaches and prints readings with alerts and a summary.
